channel.title: J.M. Struijk on ADHD and autism
channel.description: Practical writing on ADHD, autism, and AuDHD from a late-diagnosed author.

item.title: The ADHD tax: what it actually costs, and why budgeting advice keeps missing it
item.description: The ADHD tax is the money you lose to late fees, forgotten subscriptions and replacing things you already owned. Here is where it goes and why ordinary budgeting advice does not touch it.

item.title: Why ADHD brains overspend, and what actually helps
item.description: Impulsive spending with ADHD is rarely about wanting things. It is about how reward, time and emotion work in an ADHD brain, and the fixes that follow from that are different.

item.title: ADHD and debt: why payoff plans keep failing, and what to do instead
item.description: Debt payoff plans assume consistency, which is the one thing ADHD does not reliably supply. Here is why the standard methods break down and how to build one that survives a bad month.

item.title: Hyperfocus without the crash: using the good days without paying for them twice
item.description: Hyperfocus is the part of ADHD people call a superpower, usually right before it costs them a week. Here is how it actually works and how to use it without the crash that follows.

item.title: Diagnosed with ADHD as an adult: what the first year is actually like
item.description: Relief, grief, and a strange period of rereading your own life. An honest account of what tends to happen in the first year after a late ADHD diagnosis, and what helps.

item.title: Finding out you are autistic in adulthood
item.description: What changes when you discover in your thirties or forties that you are autistic, why so many people are missed, and what the first months of knowing tend to involve.

item.title: AuDHD: what it is like being autistic and ADHD at the same time
item.description: AuDHD means being both autistic and ADHD. The two sets of needs pull against each other constantly, which is why advice written for either one alone tends not to work.

item.title: Autistic burnout, ADHD burnout and depression: telling them apart
item.description: They look similar from outside and need almost opposite responses. How autistic burnout, ADHD burnout and depression differ, and why getting the distinction wrong costs so much time.

item.title: Masking, and what it costs
item.description: Masking is the constant work of appearing normal, and most people who do it stopped noticing years ago. What it is, why it is so expensive, and how unmasking actually tends to go.

item.title: Meal paralysis: why you forget to eat, then cannot decide what to eat
item.description: Standing in front of a full fridge, hungry, unable to pick anything. Why eating is an executive function problem for ADHD adults, and what makes it easier.

item.title: The 2 a.m. spiral: why ADHD overthinking happens at night
item.description: Replaying a conversation from 2014 at two in the morning. Why the ADHD overthinking spiral happens when it does, why reasoning with it fails, and what interrupts it.

item.title: Decision paralysis: why small choices cost the most
item.description: Why an ADHD brain can make a hard decision quickly and then lose forty minutes to choosing a bin bag. How analysis paralysis works and what gets you unstuck.
